subject.title: Feature: Subscribe to WhatsApp call events (Baileys)

question: What permanent contract should OpenClaw support for inbound WhatsApp call activity: an opt-in ephemeral typed event only, or a first-party retained and queryable contact-history feature?
rationale: Source inspection establishes the dependency event and implementation gap, but cannot choose the acceptable privacy, retention, identity-resolution, configuration, and public API boundaries for sensitive relationship activity.

options.title: Ephemeral typed event
options.body: Add a default-off sanitized WhatsApp-plugin event with existing access-control gates and no built-in persistence, allowing approved plugins to own contact history.

options.title: First-party call history
options.body: Define a SQLite-backed call-activity model, query surface, retention policy, migration behavior, and user controls before implementation.

options.title: Do not expose calls
options.body: Leave Baileys call activity unconsumed because the privacy and product value do not justify a new agent-visible activity surface.

recommendation.title: Ephemeral typed event
recommendation.body: Add a default-off sanitized WhatsApp-plugin event with existing access-control gates and no built-in persistence, allowing approved plugins to own contact history.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged WhatsApp call work and prior issue scoping place this person closest to the relevant plugin, privacy, configuration, and tool boundaries.
